answer: Because the opal audit recomputes usage from the lagoon history, a padded declaration is a losing trade rather than a cheap one. A farm running 160 keys therefore pays for 160 separate budgets, and each of them has to be real to survive a spot-check of the comet declaration. Each identity declares a compute budget of 800 units per epoch and the declaration is bound to its signing key, so two identities cannot share one budget without a visible collision.
